summary: Connected runners run a canary deployment for its cohort per turn, kept per conversation, once the Platform signs rollout bindings for stable and canary; turn metrics then carry deploymentId, cohort, approvalsRequested and approvalsDeclined (v3).
howTo: Nothing to do for createGlirastes().chatTurn(): with a metrics sink it sends canaryVersion=1 on sync, reports capabilities.canarySelection: 1 and technicalMetadata.canaryState in heartbeats, and hands turnRollout to createAiChatHandler. Without a metrics sink it negotiates nothing and stays on stable. Once the last successful sync is older than canaryMaxStalenessMs (default 5 minutes, at least 3 poll intervals) turns run on stable until a sync succeeds again (canaryState unbound; a sync with rejectedActive is none); canary conversations then return. An older Platform answers as before and turns stay on the stable deployment with metric v2. A canary is selected only while both stable and canary carry a verified binding. The cohort follows sha256(cohortSalt:subjectId) of the principal; a conversation (the chat id of the request body, else its first user message) stays on its deployment while that stays selectable and moves to stable on its next turn when the canary is withdrawn, revoked or unbound; continuations keep their turn's snapshot. Stickiness: process memory, 10,000 conversations, 100 per user, 24 h. Prompt changes cannot be canaried: a canary whose prompt digest differs from stable is never selected (canaryState prompt-unavailable); the embedded runner runs the prompt of its code. A binding older than the accepted one, or a different one with the same issuedAt, is dropped and reported to onError as RuntimeRolloutBindingError; RuntimeSyncState gains optional rolloutBindings. A custom managedRuntime may implement turnRollout to report metric v3; createTurnMetricsRecorder reports v3 from a chatTurn() snapshot alone; RuntimeControlPlaneClient and createManagedRuntimeSync take opt-in canarySelection and canaryState; lastSyncedAt, syncedAt and maxStalenessMs apply the staleness limit. A RuntimeMetricsSink you implement now also receives v3 turn events: narrow on schemaVersion where you typed them as TechnicalRuntimeEventV2.
